--- title: Security model and limits description: Who Nod trusts with what, the rules its server enforces, the limits of those rules, and how to report a vulnerability. sidebar: order: 13 --- This page sets out who Nod trusts with what, which rules the server enforces, and what those rules don't cover. It's written for security reviewers. For data flows and threats, see the [Security review guide](/trust/security-review/). ## Who holds what authority | Part | What it can do | What it's trusted with | | ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | You | Ask for work, approve actions, choose accounts, change permissions | Everything | | Nod server | Hold keys, check policy, decrypt values, record every use | Keys and secret values | | Browser provider | Check field origins and pages, enter values, submit | Secret values during entry | | 1Password helper | Read the logins 1Password would fill on the website in front of you, and copy the one you pick | Your 1Password account, from your approval until it is idle for 10 minutes | | Model | Plan, choose accounts, fields and buttons | Account names, statuses and website results | | Checker | Decide each app action and browser step from your messages or a schedule's or standing instruction | Your recent messages, or a schedule's saved owner inputs, corrections, bound proposals and complete instruction approval, or your standing instruction; your current rules; and the action. Earlier owner context can explain references but cannot grant another action. For a browser step: the website, page address, control label, the form a click or Enter sends, dialog text or file, what Nod typed or set; never the page's text | | Website | Receive what's submitted to its origin | The values entered on it | ## Trust boundaries ```mermaid flowchart LR you([You]):::accent --> server[Nod server
keys and policy]:::accent server <--> model[Model provider] server --> sandbox[Workspace
no keys]:::muted server --> browser[Browser
private entry] server --> db[(Database
encrypted Vault)] browser --> sites[Websites] server --> apps[Connected apps] ``` Only the server holds keys and decides what runs. The model, the workspace and anything the browser loads are on the other side of that line. ## Rules the server enforces ### Authority - Only your messages, a schedule's instruction, your standing instruction, your rules and your approvals carry authority. Pages, emails, files and tool results can't create permission. - To run an action, the checker must quote the words that allow it. The server checks those words are in what the checker was shown, and asks you when they aren't. Usage shows them next to the action. - App actions beyond reads and drafts need a review match against your request or your yes. See [Approvals](/trust/approvals/). - A confirmation is bound to the exact action and arguments, and runs once. - Background work Nod starts itself reads and drafts, and does only what your [standing instruction](/trust/approvals/#standing-instructions) asks. Anything else waits for your yes unless one of your [rules](/trust/approvals/#your-rules) allows it, a rule to ask first makes Nod ask even when the instruction covers the action, and a payment always needs your approval. ### Secrets - No tool returns a saved password, code or card to the model. - Nod is told never to ask for a password, code, card or API key in chat; it opens private entry instead. While a verification code is pending in the conversation that asked for it, only a message that is the code by itself, 4–8 digits (0–9), is taken as the code. Any other message with a number of three or more digits is refused, whatever its wording or language, unless the number follows letters without a space and doesn't end the message, as in "SKU1042 arrived". Nod asks you to send the code by itself. While a card's security code is pending, only a code sent by itself or labeled CVV, CVC or security code, as in "my CVC is 123", is taken, and any other message with a 3- or 4-digit number is refused. A code sent as a reply to a closed request, or by itself or at the end of a message until 10 minutes after Nod starts on a newer message, is refused too. None of these reach the model. Digits in other scripts and any other secret you type into chat reach the model. - Known secret values are removed from tool output and masked in screenshots. Missing token values in an older saved sign-in do not stop removal of the other known secrets. - Provider keys never enter the workspace, the browser or a prompt. ### Browser - A login is entered only into a field whose real frame origin matches the login's exact origin. Card fields must match the approved destinations. - Entry and submission happen in one step that the model can't observe or act during. Scripts on the destination page can read the entered values, as with any form. - A page changed by the model's own JavaScript must reload before entry. After a failed entry, the model's view stays locked until the filled page changes. - After Nod fills a private value on a page, the model's page scripts stay paused on that page until it reloads or moves on, so a script can't read the value back even once the field is gone. - The browser and the web tools reach only public addresses, never the host, the local network or other containers. The address is checked when each connection opens, so a name can't switch to a private address after the check. Nod drops any proxy for a web tool, whether the model names it or the web extension's settings set it. ### One use - Every private entry and payment is claimed once before browser work starts. It never runs twice, and an interrupted one becomes uncertain. See [One use, one result](/trust/outcomes/). ### Isolation - The workspace runs as an unprivileged user with no host home folder, Docker socket, provider keys, access key or browser profiles. - A connected command-line tool's token reaches only a sealed install of its declared source, run as its own user with a clean environment, apart from other tools. - [Local files](/connect/local-files/) run in the server process, only in the desktop app, and only in work whose chain of turns starts with an owner message or a schedule the owner set up; work Nod starts on its own reaches no file. Paths are checked after links are followed and must stay in the home folder or on an external drive, never in hidden files, Library or AppData, files named like secrets, Nod's own data or a folder on the owner's keep-out list. Nod can add to that list; only the owner removes entries. Listing is a read, and opening a file needs the owner's words in the trust check. Nod never changes executable files, files reach the workspace only when Nod copies them there, and nothing is deleted outright. - Every query and route is scoped to one owner. - File previews never run a file in Nod's own page. HTML runs in a sandboxed frame inside a second sandboxed frame. The outer frame blocks navigation requests from the inner frame before they leave. Its content policy also blocks external resources. It runs Nod's handlers even when scripts in the file are disabled. Interactive HTML can run local scripts, but forms and pop-ups are blocked. When file scripts are disabled, links you select can open a new window outside the preview. The preview closes after a blocked navigation. Other formats are read as data. Files that can run code get no local preview before they upload. ### Client access - Desktop windows use process sandboxing and context isolation, with Node integration and webviews disabled. Packaged windows disable DevTools and remote debugging switches. - Desktop setup uses a private protocol that serves only its five UI files. Its session denies permission requests, and its content policy blocks network access. Chat allows audio recording, clipboard writes, and notifications only from its owned main frame. Native notifications keep the app's existing controls. - Packaged chat pages limit external scripts and connections to the selected server. Their content policy permits inline scripts in the chat page, so it does not block inline script injection. This keeps sandboxed HTML previews and stickers working. Those frames have separate policies that block network access. The policy blocks plugins and code evaluation. Map frames use OpenStreetMap. - Desktop builds enable cookie encryption and disable Node option injection, Node inspector flags, and extra file-protocol privileges. Audio decoding still needs Node child processes. - Loopback isn't treated as identity. Local `/api` requests need the owner key from `NOD_DATA_ROOT/access-key`, or the local desktop app's per-launch token. A self-hosted server uses `NOD_AUTH_TOKEN`, presented by desktop clients as a bearer token and exchanged for an access cookie by web clients. Verified webhooks, OAuth callbacks, the key exchange and the privacy notice don't require the owner's access cookie. - Server app sign-in pages use a separate, expiring capability issued when an authenticated owner starts a connection. They don't require the owner's access cookie. Each page opens once, binds the connection to a private browser key, and accepts messages only from its own sign-in window at the connection service's exact origin. The capability grants no access to other API routes. - Network access requires an explicit server token and HTTPS. The server checks the request's host and browser origin against its configured public address. ## Limits :::caution[What these rules don't cover] - The server and browser provider can read secret values. There's no isolated key service or hardware-backed key release. - The website receives what's submitted, and can store, encode or show it again. Masking replaces only the exact known values. - The model can type any value it knows into a page, including a secret you typed into chat. - Nod gives each email in app results and connected-app events its own privacy decision, using a decision model or the connection's smaller model, and hides any that gives access to an account: codes, magic sign-in links, reset links, passwords, recovery codes and keys sent by email. An ordinary sign-in page link does not itself give access. A security warning without an access secret stays available for Nod to inspect, including a warning that could be phishing. The check reads the sender, subject, HTML link destinations and up to 8,000 characters of text (the start and end of a longer email), so it can miss access in the middle of a very long message, and an email downloaded as a file isn't checked. Each record is checked on its own. Nod does not reuse a decision from an earlier read. A missing, invalid or failed decision hides that record. - Once signed in, Nod can act anywhere on that website. Vault doesn't review each click. The trust check judges a browser step from what it does (a click, a key press or a script), the website and page, the control's label when there is one, the method and address of a form it sends, any dialog text or file name, and what Nod typed. It never sees the page's text. A deceptive site can still mislabel a control that acts through page scripts, or send a form to an address that doesn't say what it does. A request to buy or book covers the steps it needs on the website it names, including a control without a label when even the worst it could do there stays within the request. - A login with an authenticator key keeps both sign-in steps in Vault, so anyone who can open your Vault can complete that two-step sign-in. Add a key only where you want Nod to sign in on its own. - 1Password's approval isn't narrower than your account: until it's idle for 10 minutes or you lock 1Password, Nod's helper could read any item. Nod's code asks it only for the logins for the website in front of you and the one you pick. - The checker can be wrong in every mode. A decision model can give incorrect permission or select an incorrect source with a high probability. A probability threshold or a local classifier cannot guarantee safety. No checker is immune to prompt injection. See [Select the action checker](/connect/models/#select-the-action-checker). - Private preparation screens each changed record on its own with the connection's smaller model. A record it wrongly judges routine gets no preparation until it changes again. - Nod writes [learned skills](/how-it-works/memory/#learned-skills) from what it did and read, so a page or an email can shape one, and a skill can steer later tasks. A skill never grants permission, and the trust check never sees it. - A standing instruction runs for any new email or update that matches it, including one that only claims to come from the sender you named. Your rules apply in every kind of work, so background work started by such an email can do what a rule to go ahead covers. - The checker quotes your words, or says "read", to run an action. The server verifies that the words exist, not that they really ask for the action; that judgment is still the checker's. - Browser snapshots and typing without submitting do not need an action check. Source installs and self-hosted servers block private and reserved workspace addresses. The desktop runtime does too. Public internet access can still send data outside Nod. - A saved card can't make the issuer enforce the amount, and card support isn't a PCI DSS compliance claim. - HTML that you download and open outside Nod does not have Nod's preview protections. - Tests cover known failure cases. They don't prove that every injection or browser exploit is blocked. ::: ## Report a vulnerability Report it privately through [GitHub private vulnerability reporting](https://github.com/n8n-io/nod/security/advisories/new), or through [n8n's Vulnerability Disclosure Program](https://n8n.io/report-a-vulnerability/). Don't open a public issue, and never include real passwords, keys or other people's data. The team aims to acknowledge your report within 3 business days and to share a first assessment within 10 business days. Confirmed issues get a GitHub security advisory. Read the full [security policy](https://github.com/n8n-io/nod/blob/main/SECURITY.md) for scope and research rules. ## Where this is enforced | Area | Source | | --------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Authority and confirmations | [`trust.ts`](https://github.com/n8n-io/nod/blob/main/src/server/trust.ts), [`approvals.ts`](https://github.com/n8n-io/nod/blob/main/src/server/approvals.ts) | | Vault and one use | [`vault-access.ts`](https://github.com/n8n-io/nod/blob/main/src/server/vault-access.ts), [`vault-use.ts`](https://github.com/n8n-io/nod/blob/main/src/server/vault-use.ts) | | Browser entry and proxy | [`agent-browser`](https://github.com/n8n-io/nod/tree/main/src/providers/agent-browser) | | Client access | [`access.ts`](https://github.com/n8n-io/nod/blob/main/src/server/access.ts), [`network.ts`](https://github.com/n8n-io/nod/blob/main/src/server/network.ts) | | Local files | [`local-files.ts`](https://github.com/n8n-io/nod/blob/main/src/server/local-files.ts) | | File previews | [`attachment-frame.tsx`](https://github.com/n8n-io/nod/blob/main/src/web/components/attachment-frame.tsx), [`attachment-kind.ts`](https://github.com/n8n-io/nod/blob/main/src/web/lib/attachment-kind.ts) | ## Saved owner instructions Chat, tasks and schedules use one server record for owner evidence. Each message keeps its identity and time. A reply keeps the exact proposal it answers. Background cannot grant permission. Each checker mode receives the same evidence roles. Internal owner, turn and run IDs stay on the server. For an instruction update, the checker sees the current definition, requested field changes and complete proposed result. The writer saves the changed definition and its evidence together under the turn lock. It checks the target version and owner-input version again. An older proposal cannot overwrite a newer owner correction. Notification and lasting-rule changes also refuse a stale reviewed value. A complete schedule approval is bound to the exact future work described in its question. The writer and its separate fact check must describe its targets, timing and limits. Hidden values in that complete instruction prevent the question from being asked. A metadata approval changes only its named fields. Each later outside action still passes Trust. An approval of one outside action never becomes recurring permission. Each run keeps its execution request, run time and owner-evidence copy. Missing or withdrawn required sources refuse the work; they do not restore older grants. A complete replacement can establish a new instruction. The server does not summarize permission or erase it after a fixed number of changes. A request that exceeds the selected provider's input context limit fails without saving the update. Existing schedules migrate their known instruction without guessed context. Old correction lists have no complete source records and require a complete replacement instruction. Source checks establish where evidence came from. A model still judges whether that evidence covers the action, which corrections apply, and whether background describes the same work. A valid quote alone does not establish permission. ## Related resources - [Trust and Vault](/trust/) - [Security review guide](/trust/security-review/) - [Our trust principles](/trust/principles/) - [Your data and privacy](/trust/privacy/)

name: Security analysis

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '37 6 * * 1'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: security-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  semgrep:
    name: Semgrep
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 15
    container:
      image: semgrep/semgrep:1.179.0@sha256:93963d9295a366f59e4850127b1550400ee7b388f04fe144e4a1f6325d96e01b
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Check source for security errors
        run: semgrep scan --config p/ci --severity ERROR --metrics off --disable-version-check --error .

  codeql:
    name: CodeQL (${{ matrix.language }})
    if: ${{ !github.event.repository.private || vars.NOD_PRIVATE_CODEQL == 'true' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: read
      security-events: write
      actions: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        language: [javascript-typescript, python]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: github/codeql-action/init@33d7b85da1a04171e211befe2c739303b9a4c066
        with:
          languages: ${{ matrix.language }}
          build-mode: none
      - uses: github/codeql-action/analyze@33d7b85da1a04171e211befe2c739303b9a4c066

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  merge_group:
    types: [checks_requested]
  schedule:
    - cron: '17 3 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && 'scheduled' || (github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.sha || github.ref) }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  scope:
    name: Select checks for changed files
    runs-on: blacksmith-2vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 5
    outputs:
      types: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.types }}
      build: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.build }}
      integration: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.integration }}
      desktop: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.desktop }}
      macos: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.macos }}
      windows: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.windows }}
      n8n: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.n8n }}
      evals: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.evals }}
      images: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.images }}
      network: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.network }}
      ci: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.ci }}
      test_files: ${{ steps.scope.outputs.test_files }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1
        with:
          node-version: '24.21.0'
      - name: Read the changed paths
        id: scope
        env:
          CI_DIFF_BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.merge_group.base_sha || github.event.before || '' }}
        run: node .github/scripts/ci-scope.mjs

  notes:
    name: Delete Git notes
    needs: scope
    if: ${{ !cancelled() && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Delete every notes ref on GitHub
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/matching-refs/notes/" --jq '.[].ref' |
            while read -r ref; do
              gh api --method DELETE "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/git/$ref"
              echo "Deleted $ref"
            done

  quality:
    name: Formatting, types and client build
    needs: scope
    runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: Check out source
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          fetch-depth: ${{ (github.head_ref == 'release/desktop' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/release/desktop') && '0' || '1' }}
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Install tooling and dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-node
      - name: Check CI selection and required results
        run: node --test .github/scripts/ci-scope.test.mjs
      - name: Check formatting
        run: pnpm run format:check
      - name: Check types and import boundaries
        if: needs.scope.outputs.types == 'true'
        run: pnpm run lint
      - name: Build the web and desktop clients
        if: needs.scope.outputs.build == 'true'
        run: pnpm exec vite build && node desktop/scripts/build-ui.mjs
      - name: Check the release version and source
        if: >-
          (github.event_name == 'pull_request' &&
           github.head_ref == 'release/desktop' &&
           github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository) ||
          github.ref == 'refs/heads/release/desktop'
        run: node .github/scripts/prepare-desktop-release.mjs --check
      - name: Install verified actionlint 1.7.12
        if: needs.scope.outputs.ci == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/actionlint"
          gh release download v1.7.12 --repo rhysd/actionlint --pattern actionlint_1.7.12_linux_amd64.tar.gz --output "$RUNNER_TEMP/actionlint.tar.gz"
          printf '%s  %s\n' '8aca8db96f1b94770f1b0d72b6dddcb1ebb8123cb3712530b08cc387b349a3d8' "$RUNNER_TEMP/actionlint.tar.gz" | sha256sum --check --status
          tar --extract --gzip --file "$RUNNER_TEMP/actionlint.tar.gz" --directory "$RUNNER_TEMP/actionlint" actionlint
      - name: Check workflow syntax and expressions
        if: needs.scope.outputs.ci == 'true'
        run: >-
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/actionlint/actionlint" -shellcheck= -pyflakes=
          -ignore 'label "blacksmith-.*" is unknown'
          -ignore 'unexpected key "queue" for "concurrency" section'

  integration:
    name: Linux integration tests
    needs: scope
    if: needs.scope.outputs.integration == 'true'
    runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 20
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:17-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: nod
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: nod-ci
          POSTGRES_DB: nod_ci
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -U nod -d nod_ci"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 12
    env:
      CI: 'true'
      TEST_DATABASE_URL: postgresql://nod:nod-ci@127.0.0.1:5432/nod_ci
    steps:
      - name: Check out source
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Set up the integration image cache
        uses: useblacksmith/setup-docker-builder@06dd9c83a5d541274d2e3ac67625560979275267
        with:
          cache-key: n8n-io/nod/ci-integration
      - name: Build the integration fixture
        run: docker buildx build --load --platform linux/amd64 --file scripts/Dockerfile.integration --tag nod-ci-integration .
      - name: Build the web fixture and run the selected tests
        env:
          NOD_TEST_FILES: ${{ needs.scope.outputs.test_files }}
        run: >-
          docker run --rm --network host --shm-size=1g
          --env TEST_DATABASE_URL
          --env NOD_TEST_FILES
          --env NOD_TEST_NATIVE_DOWNLOAD=true
          --env NOD_TEST_BROWSER_EXECUTABLE=/usr/bin/chromium
          --volume "$PWD/src:/app/src:ro"
          --volume "$PWD/tests:/app/tests:ro"
          --volume "$PWD/scripts:/app/scripts:ro"
          --volume "$PWD/public:/app/public:ro"
          --volume "$PWD/desktop/main:/app/desktop/main:ro"
          --volume "$PWD/desktop/preload:/app/desktop/preload:ro"
          --volume "$PWD/desktop/ui:/app/desktop/ui:ro"
          --volume "$PWD/deployment/self-host:/app/deployment/self-host:ro"
          --volume "$PWD/tsconfig.json:/app/tsconfig.json:ro"
          --volume "$PWD/vite.config.ts:/app/vite.config.ts:ro"
          --volume "$PWD/index.html:/app/index.html:ro"
          --tmpfs /app/.local:uid=1000,gid=1000
          --tmpfs /app/dist:uid=1000,gid=1000
          --tmpfs /app/node_modules/.vite-temp:uid=1000,gid=1000
          --init --entrypoint sh nod-ci-integration
          -c 'node_modules/.bin/vite build && node scripts/test-integration.mjs --run'

  desktop:
    name: Desktop contracts and network isolation
    needs: scope
    if: needs.scope.outputs.desktop == 'true'
    runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - name: Check out source
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Install tooling and dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-node
      - name: Install desktop tooling without downloading Electron
        env:
          ELECTRON_SKIP_BINARY_DOWNLOAD: '1'
        run: pnpm --dir desktop install --frozen-lockfile
      - name: Check desktop lifecycle, storage and release contracts
        run: pnpm run desktop:test
      - name: Check desktop network isolation during restart
        if: needs.scope.outputs.network == 'true'
        run: >-
          sudo env NOD_TEST_RUNTIME_NETWORK=1 "$(command -v node)"
          --test --test-name-pattern='workload firewall refresh'
          desktop/test/runtime-assets.test.mjs

  evals:
    name: Eval harness contracts
    needs: scope
    if: needs.scope.outputs.evals == 'true'
    runs-on: blacksmith-2vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 10
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:17-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: nod
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: nod-ci
          POSTGRES_DB: nod_ci
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -h 127.0.0.1 -U nod -d nod_ci"
          --health-interval 5s
          --health-timeout 5s
          --health-retries 12
    env:
      CI: 'true'
      TEST_DATABASE_URL: postgresql://nod:nod-ci@127.0.0.1:5432/nod_ci
    steps:
      - name: Check out source
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Install tooling and dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-node
      - name: Check the eval harness with disposable schemas
        run: |
          pnpm --dir evals run check
          pnpm --dir evals test

  n8n:
    name: n8n delivery contracts
    needs: scope
    if: needs.scope.outputs.n8n == 'true'
    runs-on: blacksmith-2vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - name: Check out source
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Install tooling and dependencies
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-node
      - name: Check n8n delivery contracts
        run: node --test deployment/n8n/*.test.mjs

  images:
    name: Container and self-host checks
    needs: scope
    if: needs.scope.outputs.images == 'true'
    runs-on: blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404
    timeout-minutes: 25
    steps:
      - name: Check out source
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1

services:
  server:
    build:
      context: ../..
      dockerfile: deployment/self-host/Dockerfile
    image: nod-server:${NOD_IMAGE_TAG:-local}
    restart: unless-stopped
    init: true
    env_file: ${NOD_ENV_FILE:-.env}
    environment:
      NODE_ENV: production
      NOD_ENVIRONMENT: production
      NOD_HOST: 0.0.0.0
      PORT: ${PORT:-4310}
      NOD_DATA_ROOT: /var/lib/nod
      NOD_PUBLIC_URL: ${NOD_PUBLIC_URL:-http://localhost:${PORT:-4310}}
      NOD_AUTH_TOKEN: [REDACTED] sh setup.sh first}
      NOD_VAULT_KEY: ${NOD_VAULT_KEY:?Run sh setup.sh first}
      DATABASE_URL: ${DATABASE_URL:-postgresql://nod:${NOD_POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?Run sh setup.sh first}@postgres:5432/nod}
      DOCKER_HOST: tcp://runtime:2375
      WORKSPACE_CONTAINER: nod-workspace-${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME:-nod-server}
      BROWSER_CONTAINER: nod-browser-${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME:-nod-server}
    ports:
      - '${NOD_BIND_ADDRESS:-127.0.0.1}:${PORT:-4310}:${PORT:-4310}'
    volumes:
      - server-data:/var/lib/nod
      - workspace-data:/var/lib/nod/workspaces
    tmpfs:
      - /tmp:uid=1000,gid=1000,mode=1777,size=256m
    read_only: true
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    security_opt: [no-new-privileges:true]
    pids_limit: 512
    mem_limit: ${NOD_SERVER_MEMORY:-2g}
    networks: [backend, control, outbound]
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      runtime:
        condition: service_started
      browser:
        condition: service_healthy
      workspace:
        condition: service_started
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD', 'node', '/app/healthcheck.mjs']
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 6s
      retries: 10
      start_period: 60s

  postgres:
    image: postgres:17-alpine@sha256:eee6c6e1b0894fa4fe0075eb054af9fd1cf39a35321c2d4110626cfe506411fb
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: nod
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: [REDACTED] sh setup.sh first}
      POSTGRES_DB: nod
    volumes:
      - postgres-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    networks: [backend]
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD-SHELL', 'pg_isready -U nod -d nod']
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 30

  runtime:
    image: node:24.21.0-bookworm-slim@sha256:d6aa754f16b3197301076f047b5def2f02ea1dbbc2ca920407d46d7ec7f87b20
    restart: unless-stopped

    environment:

      - ./docker-proxy.mjs:/app/docker-proxy.mjs:ro
    networks: [control]
    read_only: true
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    security_opt: [no-new-privileges:true]
    pids_limit: 64
    mem_limit: 128m

  browser:
    build:
      context: ../..
      dockerfile: Dockerfile.browser

    security_opt: [no-new-privileges:true]

    networks: [browser]
    healthcheck:
      test:
        [
          'CMD',
          'node',
          '-e',
          'const s=require("node:net").connect("/data/control.sock");s.on("connect",()=>{s.end();process.exit(0)});s.on("error",()=>process.exit(1))',

      timeout: 3s
      retries: 30

  workspace:

    image: nod-workspace:${NOD_IMAGE_TAG:-local}
    container_name: nod-workspace-${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME:-nod-server}
    restart: unless-stopped
    init: true
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    security_opt: [no-new-privileges:true]
    pids_limit: 512
    mem_limit: ${NOD_WORKSPACE_MEMORY:-2g}
    volumes:
      - workspace-data:/workspace
      - workspace-tools:/home/node
    network_mode: service:workspace-network
    depends_on:
      workspace-network:
        condition: service_healthy
        restart: true
    command: ['sleep', 'infinity']

  workspace-network:
    image: nod-workspace:${NOD_IMAGE_TAG:-local}
    pull_policy: never
    dns: [1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8]
    user: root
    restart: unless-stopped
    init: true
    entrypoint: /usr/local/bin/nod-workspace-network
    cap_drop: [ALL]
    cap_add: [NET_ADMIN]
    security_opt: [no-new-privileges:true]
    read_only: true
    tmpfs:
      - /tmp:size=1m
    pids_limit: 32
    mem_limit: 64m
    networks: [workspace]
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD', 'test', '-f', '/tmp/network-ready']
      interval: 2s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10

  https:
    image: caddy:2.11.7-alpine@sha256:eb4d35b7452d1ab6171fbdbe8d9275b2301dad6dad92115d91e19fb9b24d510f
    profiles: [https]
    restart: unless-stopped
    entrypoint: /bin/sh
    command:
      - -ec
      - |
        origin=$${NOD_PUBLIC_URL%/}
        case "$$origin" in
          https://*) authority=$${origin#https://} ;;
          *) echo 'The HTTPS profile requires an https:// origin on port 443.' >&2; exit 1 ;;
        esac
        case "$$authority" in
          ''|*[!a-zA-Z0-9.-]*) echo 'The HTTPS profile requires a DNS or IPv4 host on port 443. Use an existing proxy for other ports or IPv6.' >&2; exit 1 ;;
        esac
        exec caddy run --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile --adapter caddyfile
    environment:
      NOD_PUBLIC_URL: ${NOD_PUBLIC_URL:-http://localhost:${PORT:-4310}}
      PORT: ${PORT:-4310}
    ports:
      - '80:80'
      - '443:443'
      - '443:443/udp'
    volumes:
      - ./Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro
      - https-data:/data
      - https-config:/config
    networks: [outbound]
    depends_on:
      server:
        condition: service_healthy
    healthcheck:
      test: ['CMD', 'wget', '-q', '-O', '/dev/null', 'http://127.0.0.1:2019/config/']
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 6

networks:

    internal: true
  outbound:
  browser:
  workspace:

volumes:

#!/bin/sh
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
umask 077
case "${1:-}" in '') [ "$#" -eq 0 ] ;; --https) [ "$#" -eq 1 ] ;; *) echo 'Usage: sh install.sh [--https]' >&2; exit 1 ;; esac
[ "${NOD_ENV_FILE:-.env}" = .env ] || { echo 'Keep configuration in this installation .env; unset NOD_ENV_FILE.' >&2; exit 1; }
if [ -f .env ] && grep -Eq '^[[:space:]]*(export[[:space:]]+)?NOD_ENV_FILE[[:space:]]*=' .env; then
  echo 'Remove NOD_ENV_FILE from .env before installing.' >&2
  exit 1
fi
if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  checksum() { sha256sum "$1" | awk '{print $1}'; }
else
  command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo 'Install sha256sum or shasum first.' >&2; exit 1; }
  checksum() { shasum -a 256 "$1" | awk '{print $1}'; }
fi
[ -f checksums.sha256 ] && [ ! -L checksums.sha256 ] || { echo 'Missing bundle checksums.' >&2; exit 1; }
for file in .env.example Caddyfile docker-proxy.mjs setup.sh backup.sh restore.sh install.sh compose.yaml source-revision architecture images.txt images.tar.gz; do
  [ -f "$file" ] && [ ! -L "$file" ] || { echo "Missing regular bundle file: $file" >&2; exit 1; }
  expected=$(awk -v name="$file" '$2 == name {print $1}' checksums.sha256)
  [ "${#expected}" -eq 64 ] && [ "$(checksum "$file")" = "$expected" ] || { echo "Bundle checksum failed: $file" >&2; exit 1; }
done
revision=$(cat source-revision)
[ "${#revision}" -eq 40 ] || { echo 'Invalid source revision.' >&2; exit 1; }
case "$revision" in *[!a-f0-9]*) echo 'Invalid source revision.' >&2; exit 1 ;; esac
architecture=$(cat architecture)
case "$architecture" in amd64|arm64) ;; *) echo 'Unsupported bundle architecture.' >&2; exit 1 ;; esac
platform=$(docker info --format '{{.OSType}}/{{.Architecture}}')
case "$platform" in linux/x86_64|linux/amd64) native=amd64 ;; linux/aarch64|linux/arm64) native=arm64 ;; *) echo 'Use a Linux Docker Engine on AMD64 or ARM64.' >&2; exit 1 ;; esac
[ "$architecture" = "$native" ] || { echo "This bundle is $architecture; Docker requires $native." >&2; exit 1; }
sh setup.sh >/dev/null
docker image load --input images.tar.gz >/dev/null
while read -r reference config target; do
  case "$reference" in nod-server:bundle-*|nod-browser:bundle-*|nod-workspace:bundle-*) ;; *) echo 'Invalid bundled image reference.' >&2; exit 1 ;; esac
  actual=$(docker image inspect --format '{{.Id}} {{.Os}}/{{.Architecture}} {{index .Config.Labels "org.opencontainers.image.revision"}}' "$reference")
  [ "$actual" = "$config linux/$architecture $revision" ] || [ "$actual" = "$target linux/$architecture $revision" ] || { echo 'Loaded image does not match the bundle.' >&2; exit 1; }
done < images.txt
if [ "${1:-}" = --https ]; then
  docker compose --file compose.yaml --env-file .env --profile https up -d --no-build --wait --wait-timeout 180
else
  docker compose --file compose.yaml --env-file .env up -d --no-build --wait --wait-timeout 180
fi
address=$(docker compose --file compose.yaml --env-file .env exec -T server node -p 'process.env.NOD_PUBLIC_URL')
printf 'Nod is ready at %s\n' "$address"
printf '%s\n' 'Enter NOD_AUTH_TOKEN from the private .env file. For a remote loopback address, open an SSH tunnel first.' "Installed source revision: $revision"

# n8n workflows

This folder maintains five of Nod's workflows on the internal n8n instance. Each script here generates or embeds the exact workflow source, and each has synthetic contract tests.

| Workflow               | Source                           | What it does                                                                                       |
| ---------------------- | -------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Nod Desktop Releases   | `desktop-releases.mjs`           | Serves published desktop releases, runtime packs and update feeds without exposing a GitHub token  |
| Nod Install            | `install-workflow.mjs`           | Serves `install.sh` for Mac Terminal and `install.ps1` for Windows PowerShell                      |
| Nod Feedback           | `feedback.mjs`                   | Turns in-app feedback into a Linear issue with its reports attached                                |
| Nod Traces             | `traces.mjs`                     | Forwards opted-in, scrubbed conversation traces to the `nod` LangSmith project in the EU           |
| Nod onboarding updates | `onboarding-updates.workflow.ts` | Records an unverified email signup and fixed About you choices in Customer.io Labs; sends no email |

```sh
node --test deployment/n8n/*.test.mjs
```

- The release broker only serves published `nod-v*` releases from this repository, pins each asset by release and asset ID, and never streams archives through n8n.
- The traces broker refuses requests without the `x-nod-traces-token` header from the n8n credential `nod traces webhook`, answers the rest with 202, validates each trace, forwards about 600 per clock minute in total (a best-effort cost cap: a burst across a minute boundary or simultaneous runs can pass a few more), pins each to that project by its ID as one `llm` run and keeps no execution data. Official desktop builds get the token from the `NOD_TRACES_TOKEN` release secret; anyone who unpacks the app can read it, so it keeps out scanners, not a determined sender. Its LangSmith service key lives only in the n8n credential `nod LangSmith traces`, never in Nod.
- The onboarding updates workflow exposes a public n8n webhook, accepts only versioned email submissions with a consent-checkbox claim and fixed About you choices, and rejects bodies over 2 KB after n8n parses them. Anyone can call the webhook, so the claim does not verify control of the address. The workflow stamps the receipt time on the server and identifies the person by normalized email in Customer.io Labs, where email is enabled as an identifier. Customer.io updates the existing profile or creates one if the address is new. Keep email identification enabled in Labs; otherwise the address can become a separate ID. The workflow uses the same Track API credential as Nod Waitlist, preserves unsubscribe state, and sends no message. Apply the retention settings in `onboarding-updates.settings.json` before publication. Do not send update emails until the double opt-in confirmation flow is ready.
- Feedback requests are versioned in `src/ports/feedback.ts`. The workflow checks every hash before it touches Linear, and repeated submissions with the same ID can't create a second issue. Execution data retention stays off.
- Older private builds use the release broker. Publish it before an installer that depends on it, and export the current workflow version before replacing it so you can roll back.
- Public builds and installers fetch GitHub Releases directly. Check that their installer, runtime pack, and update assets resolve before publishing a release. The n8n broker remains available for older private builds.

User-facing behaviour is documented in [Install the desktop app](../../docs/src/content/docs/get-started/install-desktop.mdx) and [Your data and privacy](../../docs/src/content/docs/trust/privacy.md).

pnpm run build
